section_summary: These pages trace Allied decisions about Japan’s new constitution, especially its later review, the announcement of that review policy, and scrutiny of laws needed to implement it. They include directives to the Supreme Commander, Far Eastern Commission records, MacArthur’s objection to early publicity, and State Department policy discussions. Other documents report the constitution’s final amendments, reactions to its promulgation, and a Chinese objection to the choice of November 3.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Directive Serial No. 60
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of a directive on further policies for Japan’s new constitution.
subfiles.summary: Sends Directive Serial No. 60 for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Further Policies Relating to a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits Far Eastern Commission policy on civilian ministers and the two houses of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Requires civilian cabinet ministers and rejects predominance of the House of Councillors over the House of Representatives.

subfiles.title: Filing of Directive Serial No. 60
subfiles.about: Files a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 60 with the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the certified directive for Commission filing.

subfiles.title: Draft Directive on Review of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a draft directive based on the Commission’s October 17 policy.
subfiles.summary: Asks that the draft be sent through the Joint Chiefs of Staff to MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Provisions for the Review of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets out review of the constitution by the Diet and Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Calls for review one to two years after the constitution takes effect and allows a referendum to establish Japanese opinion.

subfiles.title: Request to Transmit a Consultative Message
subfiles.about: Seeks MacArthur’s views on when and how to issue the constitutional review policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests Joint Chiefs transmission of the enclosed consultation message.

subfiles.title: Request for Consultation on Issuing the Review Policy
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests MacArthur’s views after Commission debate over publication of its review decision.
subfiles.summary: Records Australian, New Zealand, and United States positions and asks about the time and manner of issuance.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Constitutional Review Policy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Commission’s review policy and requests consultation with MacArthur about its issuance.
subfiles.summary: Johnson reports unanimous approval and asks the United States to transmit the decision as a directive while seeking MacArthur’s views on publication.

subfiles.title: Certification of the October 17 Policy Decision
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached Commission decision as a correct copy.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the October 17 decision.

subfiles.title: Provisions for the Review of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: Establishes later review of the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: Provides for Diet and Commission review within one to two years and permits a referendum or another test of Japanese opinion.

subfiles.title: Excerpt from the Thirtieth Commission Meeting
subfiles.about: Records debate on the timing of announcement of the constitutional review policy.
subfiles.summary: Makin and Berendsen favored early notice to Japan; McCoy urged consultation with MacArthur. The Commission unanimously adopted the policy subject to reconsidering its issuance after receiving MacArthur’s views.

subfiles.title: Return of a Message Copy Intended for the Commission
subfiles.about: Declines to circulate an explanatory United States message to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Returns the Commission copy because the message was prepared for United States government use.

subfiles.title: Clarification on Circulation of Messages
subfiles.about: Corrects a misunderstanding about whether explanatory messages should go to the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Borton says the messages should not be distributed to the Commission.

subfiles.title: Corrections to a Current Biography Article
subfiles.about: Corrects an article’s account of Atcheson, MacArthur, and Allied affairs in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson corrects titles, his Chungking service and transfer, and claims about the Allied Council and Soviet proposals. He points Rothe to official records and published statements.

subfiles.title: Question of Distributing Commentary on a Directive
subfiles.about: Asks whether commentary sent to MacArthur should receive regular Commission distribution.
subfiles.summary: Calls Penfield’s attention to copies of messages commenting on the constitutional directive.

subfiles.title: Copies of Messages to the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of October 10 and 18 messages for Commission and State Department files.
subfiles.summary: Supplies three copies of each message.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Directive Serial No. 62
subfiles.about: Forwards the directive on later review of the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Sends Directive Serial No. 62 for Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Directive Regarding Provisions for Review of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission’s policy for Diet and Allied review after the constitution takes effect.
subfiles.summary: Directs review within one to two years and permits a referendum or other procedure to assess whether the constitution reflects Japanese free will.

subfiles.title: Filing of Directive Serial No. 62
subfiles.about: Files a certified copy of the constitutional review directive.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Directive Serial No. 62 for Commission filing.

subfiles.title: Statement for Constitution Promulgation
subfiles.about: Reports a statement prepared for Asahi’s November 3 constitution supplement.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson welcomes the constitution as a framework for democracy and says its success depends on the Japanese people.

subfiles.title: Chinese Suggestion to Change the Promulgation Date
subfiles.about: Reports Chu Shih-ming’s objection to promulgating the constitution on Meiji festival day.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson summarizes Chu’s objection and his own conclusion that intervention over the date was unwarranted.

subfiles.title: Chu Shih-ming’s Objection to November 3
subfiles.about: Urges selection of another date for the constitution’s promulgation.
subfiles.summary: Chu argues that the Meiji festival evokes imperial expansion and is unsuitable for a democratic constitution.

subfiles.title: Reply on the Constitution’s Promulgation Date
subfiles.about: Explains why he opposes intervention over the November 3 promulgation date.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson links the date to Meiji’s first constitution and regards its selection as a local administrative matter.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of MacArthur’s Consultation Reply
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s answer about issuing the review policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of the attached reply to the Commission chairman.

subfiles.title: MacArthur’s Views for the Commission Chairman
subfiles.about: Forwards MacArthur’s November 1 response on public issuance of the review decision.
subfiles.summary: Asks the chairman to make MacArthur’s message available to Commission members.

subfiles.title: MacArthur’s Objection to Early Publication
subfiles.about: Opposes publicizing the review policy soon after the constitution’s adoption.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur warns that announcement could make the constitution appear imposed under Allied force and recommends waiting at least a year.

subfiles.title: Copies of the October 29 Consultative Message
subfiles.about: Forwards copies of a message sent to the Supreme Commander.
subfiles.summary: Supplies one Commission copy and two State Department copies.

subfiles.title: Consultation on Issuing the Review Decision
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Seeks MacArthur’s advice on the timing and manner of issuing the review policy.
subfiles.summary: Recounts Commission agreement to consult MacArthur before deciding when and how to announce its constitutional review decision.

subfiles.title: Commission Debate After MacArthur’s Reply
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent; Ernest A. Gross
subfiles.about: Reports divisions within the Commission over publication of the review decision.
subfiles.summary: Committee members disputed whether to direct MacArthur to inform Japan before the Diet’s special session or consult him further. Borton outlines possible United States responses, including a veto, a new consultation message, or another course.

subfiles.title: Filing of the October 29 Consultative Message
subfiles.about: Files the chairman’s October 29 message to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a certified copy for Commission files.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Corrected MacArthur Message
subfiles.about: Forwards a correction to MacArthur’s earlier message.
subfiles.summary: Sends the corrected passage for transmission to the Commission chairman.

subfiles.title: Correction to MacArthur’s Consultation Reply
subfiles.about: Corrects wording about the effect of publicizing the review decision.
subfiles.summary: Supplies replacement wording describing publicity as an implied coercive threat by Allied powers.

subfiles.title: Amendments to the Japanese Draft Constitution
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits an English translation of amendments approved by both houses of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Government Section translation of changes to the March draft.

subfiles.title: Changes Approved by the House of Representatives and House of Peers
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Lists changes made during Diet consideration of the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: The article-by-article list records changes to sovereignty, the emperor’s duties, renunciation of war, rights, the Diet, courts, local government, and other provisions. It then identifies three House of Peers additions, including universal adult suffrage and the requirement that ministers be civilians.

subfiles.title: Commission Authority Over Implementing Legislation
subfiles.about: Urges a United States position on Commission review of draft implementing laws.
subfiles.summary: Emmerson notes that Commission members expect to examine legislation before enactment while the War Department disputes that authority. He proposes a draft position allowing consistency review and closer liaison with MacArthur’s headquarters.

subfiles.title: Competence of the Commission Regarding Implementing Legislation
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Defines how the Commission could examine legislation implementing the constitution.
subfiles.summary: The study proposes that the Commission review bills after introduction into the Diet solely for consistency with the Potsdam Declaration, controlling documents, and Commission decisions. It recommends formal liaison with MacArthur’s headquarters and argues that review before enactment would avoid publicly invalidating laws passed by the Diet. Appendices compile earlier Commission discussions and explain the proposed limits.

subfiles.title: Statements on the New Constitution
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits published Allied statements marking promulgation of the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Encloses statements by Atcheson, Ball, Robertson, Shen, and MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Atcheson Statement in the Nippon Times
subfiles.about: Welcomes the constitution as a gateway to democratic government.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson stresses recent reforms and places responsibility for democracy’s future with the Japanese people.

subfiles.title: British Commonwealth Statements in the Nippon Times
subfiles.from: W. Macmahon Ball; H. C. H. Robertson
subfiles.about: Presents British Commonwealth views of the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: Ball calls promulgation an opportunity for Japan and urges other nations to help its people use the charter. Robertson welcomes its democratic rights and renunciation of war while saying Japan’s conduct will determine how the constitution is judged.

subfiles.title: Shen Statement in Asahi
subfiles.about: Offers a Chinese representative’s assessment of the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: Shen praises popular sovereignty, renunciation of war, and local autonomy while urging the Japanese people to put the charter into practice.

subfiles.title: MacArthur Statement in the Nippon Times
subfiles.about: Welcomes the constitution as a step toward peace.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur describes the charter and Diet reforms as a foundation for a new Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmission of the Policy on Communicating Review to Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Commission decision on formally informing Japan of the review policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests preparation and transmission of an implementing directive.

subfiles.title: Certification of the December 12 Policy Decision
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached Commission decision.
subfiles.summary: Certifies a true copy of the December 12 decision.

subfiles.title: Issuance of the Policy Decision on Review
subfiles.about: Calls for formal communication of the review policy to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Directs that Japan’s government be informed while public announcement remains under Commission consideration.

subfiles.title: Draft Directive on Issuing the Review Policy
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a directive implementing the December 12 decision.
subfiles.summary: Sends a draft directive for Joint Chiefs transmission to MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Communication of the Review Policy to Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs formal notice of the review policy to Japan’s government.
subfiles.summary: Calls for formal communication while reserving the question of public announcement.

subfiles.title: Approved Position on Announcement
subfiles.about: Forwards the approved United States position on publication of the review policy.
subfiles.summary: Requests that the approved conclusion be sent to the United States Commission member.

subfiles.title: Decision on SWNCC 228/12
subfiles.about: Records approval of the policy paper on announcement.
subfiles.summary: Records informal approval of SWNCC 228/12.

subfiles.title: Circulation Note for SWNCC 228/12
subfiles.about: Circulates a study of the review policy’s announcement.
subfiles.summary: Submits the State member’s study for committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Policy Toward Announcement of Constitutional Review
subfiles.about: Recommends a United States position on publication of the Commission’s review decision.
subfiles.summary: Recommends withholding agreement to publication until consultation with MacArthur shows it supports United States policy and Allied objectives.

subfiles.title: FEC-031/41: Provisions for Review of a New Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: Reproduces the Commission’s October review decision as an appendix to the policy study.
subfiles.summary: The circular records the decision’s approval and confidential circulation. Its enclosure provides for Diet and Commission review one to two years after the constitution takes effect and allows a referendum to gauge Japanese opinion.
